claims.claim: On November 17, 2026, Vancouver City Council approved permanent park status for about 31,000 square feet at 722 Gore Avenue.
claims.episode_span: approved permanent park status for about 31,000 square feet, roughly one acre, of city-owned land at 722 Gore Avenue
claims.source_title: Vancouver City Council approves permanent park status for Chinatown green space
claims.supporting_quote: On Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, the new makeup of Vancouver City Council approved the permanent park status for the roughly 31,000 sq. ft. (about one acre) of City of Vancouver-owned land at 722 Gore Ave.

claims.claim: Council unanimously approved Chloe Leslie’s motion on three SRO buildings covering 118 homes, with a staff report due by January 2027.
claims.source_title: Vancouver's new city council gets down to the business of reversing last council's decisions

claims.claim: Downtown Vancouver leased office vacancy rose from 12.2 per cent to 13.1 per cent in the third quarter of 2026 after Amazon vacated about 250,000 square feet.
claims.episode_span: pushed downtown leased-office vacancy from 12.2 per cent in the second quarter to 13.1 per cent
claims.source_title: Amazon's latest consolidation into The Post sends Downtown Vancouver office vacancy to its highest level in 22 years
claims.supporting_quote: This single move by the multinational giant — which has grown to become one of the city’s largest corporate office tenants over the past decade — pushed the leased office vacancy rate in Downtown Vancouver from 12.2 per cent in the second quarter to 13.1 per cent in the third quarter.

claims.claim: Nyx is the first electronic storage detection dog at a municipal police force in B.C. and has completed six successful searches.
claims.episode_span: she is the first at a municipal police force in British Columbia
claims.source_title: Meet Nyx, the Surrey Police Service dog who finds electronic devices
claims.supporting_quote: Nyx’s official title is “electronic storage detection dog”, and she is the first at a municipal police force in B.C.

claims.claim: Doug McCallum said Surrey council approved all 16 Safe Surrey Coalition priorities, including a five-year property-tax freeze.
claims.episode_span: the first council meeting approved all 16
claims.source_title: McCallum spoke at 11th annual Clovie awards
claims.supporting_quote: He noted during their first council meeting they approved all 16.

claims.claim: The Labour Relations Board found Teck Resources violated the labour code at Highland Valley Copper by using replacement workers for striking employees’ work.
claims.episode_span: found Teck Resources violated the provincial labour code
claims.source_title: Highland Valley Copper ordered to stop using replacement workers
claims.supporting_quote: B.C.’s Labour Relations Board has found Teck Resources violated the provincial labour code by using two promoted supervisors, a rehired retiree, and an outside contractor to do the work of striking employees during an ongoing labour dispute.

claims.claim: The Queen’s Park house at 239 Fourth Street was built in 1888 and is listed at $1.25 million after an August asking price of $1.425 million.
claims.episode_span: listed in August for $1.425 million and can be bought now for $1.25 million
claims.source_title: 138-year-old heritage home in New Westminster at risk of demolition
claims.supporting_quote: The corner-lot property was listed for sale in August for $1.425 million and can be purchased now for $1.25 million.

claims.claim: A study collected 58 humpback blow samples from 26 whales, with about 84 per cent of the DNA from the whale.
claims.source_title: Researchers on B.C. coast use drones to collect whale snot for genome sequencing
claims.supporting_quote: They collected 58 blow samples from a total of 26 humpbacks. The study said about 84 per cent of the DNA in the blow came from the whale itself.

claims.claim: Police identified the Langley burning-vehicle victim as 25-year-old Tushar Sharma of Surrey.
claims.episode_span: identified the victim as 25-year-old Tushar Sharma of Surrey
claims.source_title: Man found in burning vehicle in Langley identified by police
claims.supporting_quote: The victim has now been identified as 25-year-old Tushar Sharma of Surrey, who police say did not have a criminal record and had "limited known" contacts in Canada.

claims.claim: Surrey police said the Lord Tweedsmuir threat was unfounded and are investigating it as suspected swatting.
claims.episode_span: the threat was unfounded and is being investigated as suspected swatting
claims.source_title: Surrey's Lord Tweedsmuir secondary evacuated after threat reported
claims.supporting_quote: At this time, police are now investigating this incident as a suspected ‘swatting’ call, which is a false emergency report.

claims.claim: Valemount Mayor Owen Torgerson pleaded not guilty to one count of sexual assault.
claims.source_title: Valemount, B.C., mayor pleads not guilty to sexual assault charge
claims.supporting_quote: Mayor Owen Torgerson was charged with one count of sexual assault last month in relation to an offence that allegedly occurred at or near Valemount on April 2. He pleaded not guilty on Tuesday.

claims.claim: Highway 99 in West Vancouver is closed from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on November 18 for hazard tree removal, with a detour via Horseshoe Bay Drive.
claims.episode_span: Highway 99 in West Vancouver is closed today for hazard-tree removal
claims.source_title: DriveBC: 6 major road events in Metro Vancouver
claims.supporting_quote: Road closure. Detour in effect. Last update: November 13th, 2026 at 1:26pm PCT. Hazard tree removal. Detour via Horseshoe Bay Drive.

claims.claim: Environment Canada forecasts a Wednesday high of 11 in Vancouver with no watches or warnings in effect.
claims.episode_span: Wednesday is sunny, becoming a mix of sun and cloud this afternoon
claims.supporting_quote: Wednesday: Sunny. Becoming a mix of sun and cloud this afternoon. Wind becoming northwest 20 km/h this afternoon. High 11.

claims.claim: The Goodman Report called Sean Orr’s tenant-rights proposal a damaging ideological assault that could crush housing investment.
claims.episode_span: a damaging, ideological policy assault on the city’s landlords and investors
claims.source_title: Vancouver's new city council gets down to the business of reversing last council's decisions
claims.supporting_quote: On Monday, a local commercial real estate publication, the Goodman Report , blasted Orr’s proposal as “a damaging, ideological policy assault on the city’s landlords and investors” and a “governmental sledgehammer that could crush housing investment in the city.”
